newsitem.title: USA: Hicks Muse buys LIN Television for $1.7 billion.
newsitem.headline: Hicks Muse buys LIN Television for $1.7 billion.

text.p: Hicks, Muse, Tate & Furst Inc. said Tuesday it agreed to acquire LIN Television Corp., the owner and operator of 12 television stations, for $1.7 billion in cash and assumption of debt.

Under the deal, which has been unanimously approved by LIN's board of directors, Hicks Muse agreed to pay LIN shareholders $47.50 a share in cash, and assume $260 million of debt. Lin is 45 percent owned by AT&T Corp.

LIN, which owns and operates eight network-affiliated television stations and operates four additional stations under local management agreements, was formed in December 1994 as part of a spinoff from LIN Broadcasting Corp.
Hicks, Muse, a private investment firm, said the deal would be its largest investment since its formation in 1989.
The firm said it and LIN President and Chief Executive Gary Chapman plan to use LIN as a platform to execute further acquisitions in radio broadcasting and other industries.
LIN Television shareholders are set to vote on the merger before November 30, the firm said. If the deal is approved, it is expected to close in early 1998 and no later than May 12, 1998.
The announcement was made after the close of stock trading. Lin's shares closed at $48.625, up 75 cents, on Nasdaq.
When the transaction is completed, LIN is to retain its name, its headquarters in Providence, R.I., all station personnel and its management team, the investment firm said.

"By combining the financial and broadcasting industry expertise of Hicks Muse and LIN, we plan to capitalise on the unique and favourable conditions now present in the television broadcasting industry and be an active participant in the future of network television," Hicks Chairman and Chief Executive Thomas Hicks said in a statement.
AT&T said in December it was looking at options that could lead to its shedding its 45 percent stake, or 13.5 million shares, in LIN Television.
AT&T had acquired its stake in LIN through the September 1994 merger with McCaw Cellular Communications, which indirectly held a majority of LIN shares.

"The decision to sell LIN Television is part of our aggressive effort to ensure that AT&T's portfolio includes only businesses central to our communications services strategy," AT&T Chief Financial Officer Dan Somers said.

Meanwhile, AT&T, Hicks Muse and LIN also have an agreement under which AT&T is to sell its 100 percent owned WOOD-TV station in Grand Rapids, Mich., along with its local marketing agreement with WOTV for about $122.5 million.
